newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australians see budget strong, fair - Howard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australians see budget strong, fair - Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday he was certain that Australians accepted last week's budget as strong and fair.

Asked about surveys showing a good response to the budget, Howard told reporters: "I don't normally get euphoric about any opinion polls but I am sure that most Australians see it as a fair but strong budget, and that is what they really wanted.

"Australians understand an argument when it is put to them fairly and reasonably. They knew we had to take some difficult decisions but they see the decisions as having been fairly spread across all sections of the Australian community."
An opinion poll published in The Australian newspaper on Tuesday found most voters believed the budget, delivered last week, would be good for the economy.

The poll of 1,158 people taken last weekend found a total 59 percent believed the budget, which cut the 1996/97 deficit by A$3.9 billion, would be good for the economy while 22 percent believed it would be bad for the economy.
Another survey, the AGB-McNair poll in The Sydney Morning Herald, found 54 percent of voters describing the budget as fair and 32 percent saying it was not fair.
